newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FORECAST - Brazil January trade picture cloudy.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Brazil January trade picture cloudy.

text.p: Start-up problems with a new import registry could distort Brazil's January trade numbers and allow the government to post a slight surplus, but economists say the actual figure would be about $1.0 billion in the red.

"If the government shows a January number roughly in balance then it will be totally due to Siscomex," said Marcelo Carvalho, JP Morgan's chief economist in Brazil, referring to the new registry which began tracking imports on Jan 1.
Economists said start-up problems with Siscomex have slowed the liberation of imported goods at customs, which will artificially improve Brazil's trade balance in January.
There is talk in Brasilia of a $50 million trade surplus for January, which would be the nation's first trade surplus since May 1996.
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry is expected to release January trade numbers on Wednesday at 1100 local/1300 GMT.
Government officials have said problems early in the month with Siscomex were worked out and the January figure it posts on Wednesday will be accurate. Economists, however, disagreed.

"Essentially we are expecting to see average monthly trade deficits above $1.0 billion in the first quarter," Carvalho said. "Brazil's trade picture will be cloudy until the Siscomex distortions disappear."
Economists say January's true trade picture will not be known until the February numbers are available next month.
They noted that Brazil will probably post an unusually large trade gap in February due to January's imports being carried over this month.
A Reuter survey of eight Brazilian banks and research firms forecast a January trade gap of about $900 million. That survey did not take into consideration problems with Siscomex.
Private and government estimates point to a 1997 Brazilian trade gap of $8.0 billion, up from $5.4 billion.
